# =============================================================================
# uv override for the checkov lockfile (.github/requirements.txt)
# =============================================================================
# checkov hard-pins asteval==1.0.6 in every 3.3.x release — confirmed against
# the PyPI metadata of both 3.3.16 (the pinned version) and 3.3.19 (the latest)
# — and two advisories in asteval < 1.0.9 are reachable only through that pin:
# GHSA-89v8-rhwq-hf77 and GHSA-9w56-46f6-3qhx. Because the lockfile is
# hash-pinned, the bump is otherwise unresolvable and the two advisories would
# have to sit in .github/osv-scanner.toml as accepted risk.
#
# Forcing a fixed version keeps the lockfile honest instead of ignoring the
# advisory. 1.0.10 is the current release and predates the --exclude-newer
# cutoff in the command below, so the pin is stable under it. Consume it when
# compiling:
#
#   printf 'checkov==3.3.16\n' | uv pip compile --generate-hashes \
#     --python-version 3.11 --exclude-newer 2026-09-02T14:59:08Z \
#     --overrides .github/asteval-override.txt -o .github/requirements.txt -
#
# and install the result without re-resolving (see .github/workflows/
# security.yml), otherwise pip rejects the set as unsatisfiable:
#
#   python -m pip install --no-deps --require-hashes -r .github/requirements.txt
#
# This file must stay out of Dependabot's reach. A `pip` watch on /.github
# treats this override as a requirements file (the `==` is a valid pin), so the
# bot would rewrite the version this repository forces into the toolchain, and
# would re-resolve the whole closure without the override or the cutoff —
# landing versions that violate checkov's own declared constraints. Bumps are
# applied by hand with the command above.
#
# Re-evaluate when checkov adopts asteval >= 1.0.9: drop this file, drop
# --no-deps, and delete the two asteval IgnoredVulns entries for good.
# =============================================================================

asteval==1.0.10
